The '''Stein-Rosenberg theorem''', proved in 1948, states that under certain premises, the [[Jacobi method]] and the [[Gauss-Seidel method]] are either both convergent, or both divergent. If they are convergent, then the Gauss-Seidel is asymptotically faster than the Jacobi method.

== Statement ==

Let <math>A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}</math>. Let <math>\rho(X)</math> be the [[spectral radius]] of a matrix <math>X</math>. Let <math>T_J=D^{-1}(L+U)</math> and <math>T_1=(D-L)^{-1}U</math> be the [[matrix splitting]] for the Jacobi method and the Gauss-Seidel method respectively.

'''Theorem:''' If <math>a_{ij}\le 0</math> for <math>i\ne j</math> and <math>a_{ii} > 0</math> for <math>i=1,\ldots,n</math>. Then, one and only one of the following mutually exclusive relations is valid:
# <math>\rho(T_J) = \rho(T_1) = 0</math>.
# <math>0 < \rho(T_1) < \rho(T_J) < 1</math>.
# <math>1=\rho(T_J)=\rho(T_1)</math>.
# <math>1 < \rho(T_J) < \rho(T_1)</math>.

== Proof and applications ==

The proof uses the [[Perron-Frobenius theorem]] for non-negative matrices. Its proof can be found in [[Richard S. Varga]]'s 1962 book ''Matrix Iterative Analysis''.<ref>{{cite book |last=Varga |first=Richard S. |author-link=Richard S. Varga |title=Matrix Iterative Analysis |isbn=978-3-540-66321-8 |ol=5858659M |date=1962}}</ref>

In the words of Richard Varga:
<blockquote> the Stein-Rosenberg theorem gives us our first comparison theorem for two different iterative methods. Interpreted in a more practical way, not only is the point Gauss-Seidel iterative method computationally more convenient to use (because of storage requirements) than the point Jacobi iterative matrix, but it is also asymptotically faster when the Jacobi matrix <math>T_J</math> is non-negative
</blockquote>

Employing more hypotheses, on the matrix <math>A</math>, one can even give quantitative results. For example, under certain conditions one can state that the Gauss-Seidel method is twice as fast as the Jacobi iteration.<ref>{{cite web |date=2023-06-06 |title=Theorem of Stein and Rosenberg |url=https://eklausmeier.goip.de/blog/2023/06-06-theorem-of-stein-rosenberg/ |website=eklausmeier.goip.de}}</ref>
